rv.q: The play's tragedy strikes as deep as it does because it makes room, within and intertwined with the act of violence to which it is bearing witness, for so much beauty.
The play's simple and effective revival at the Irish Rep is directed by Doug Hughes and performed by a capable ensemble cast.

October 29, 2023 9:00 pm Translations: Finding the Meaning Behind the Words By Melissa Rose Bernardo ★★★★☆ Irish Rep kicks off its Friel Project with a revival of the playwright's 1980 language-focused, culture-clash drama In Romeo and Juliet , Shakespeare famously asks, “What’s in a name?”
It's a fascinating, if sometimes wearying, examination of a people being colonized through nonviolent means, namely by gradually replacing the native language with a foreign one.
Doug Hughes directs Friels most political work with sense and sensibility.

cn.t: Critics praise Irish Rep's revival of Friel's "Translations" as a quietly devastating and exquisite exploration of language and cultural loss in 1833 Ireland, with particular acclaim for its beautiful courtship scene and poignant examination of a people losing their identity.
